column7: Login/RefreshToken/VerifyMFA/BeginWebAuthnLogin/FinishWebAuthnLogin/FinishWebAuthnPasswordlessLogin all checked the per-IP login-attempt budget then ran the slow credential check (bcrypt/TOTP/WebAuthn assertion) and only recorded the attempt afterward, on failure only -- a concurrent burst from one IP all observed the same under-budget count at check time and blew through the budget before the counter caught up. Fixed by moving the record (renamed reserveLoginAttempt) to run before the slow step, right after the request is well-formed, at every affected call site; see docs/findings/2026-09-20-FINDING-login-lockout-mfa-recheck.md. Proving test REPOINTED by ORACLE-A-1 (#2816): this row named TestLogin_ConcurrentBurst_RateLimitBoundsCredentialChecks, whose statistical aggregate-429 assertion this PR removes as flaky-by-construction (overlapping distributions; 38 observed against a threshold of 40 under CI load). The ceiling is now asserted EXACTLY by the named test, which parks the whole per-IP budget inside its credential checks and shows the next request refused at the gate -- so the claim is proved by construction instead of by sampling. check-closures.sh would have stayed GREEN on the old name (the test still exists and passes), which is exactly why the row had to move: a closure whose proving test no longer asserts the claim is a green check that does not cover what its name implies.
